deep.reconstruction:
This folio is not a manuscript. It is page 22 of the printed text (offprint) of Riemann's paper 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 7, 1857), carrying the running head 'Zur Theorie der Gauss'schen Function'. It contains the end of Art. VIII, with a few hand marks.

Context (previous page). A P-function has exponent pairs (α,α'), (β,β'), (γ,γ') at the points 0, ∞, 1, and the six exponents sum to 1. Its branch P^α equals Const·x^α(1-x)^γ·F(α+β+γ, α+β'+γ, α-α'+1; x). Of the 8 representations of P in the variable x (exchanging paired exponents), the two that differ by β↔β' give the same series. So there are 4 series in ascending powers of x: two represent P^α (with factor (1-x)^γ or (1-x)^{γ'}) and two represent P^{α'}. These converge for |x|<1.

(1) Convergence regions. The 4 descending-power series in x (representing P^β, P^{β'}) behave the opposite way: they converge for |x|>1 and diverge for |x|<1.

(2) Boundary |x|=1. By the Fourier-series argument, a power series on its unit circle diverges if the represented function becomes infinite at x=1 of order >1. It stays convergent if the order is <1 or the function is finite.
- The series F(a,b,c;x) behaves near x=1 like (1-x)^{c-a-b}.
- [mine] For the series carrying the factor (1-x)^γ we have a=α+β+γ, b=α+β'+γ, c=α-α'+1. Then c-a-b = 1-α-α'-β-β'-2γ = γ'-γ, using α+α'+β+β'+γ+γ'=1.
- So that series converges on |x|=1 iff Re(γ'-γ) > -1. Its partner, with factor (1-x)^{γ'}, converges iff Re(γ-γ') > -1.
- Hence if Re(γ'-γ) ∉ (-1,1), exactly half of the 8 expansions in powers of x (ascending and descending) converge on |x|=1. If Re(γ'-γ) ∈ (-1,1), all of them converge.

(3) Counting the series. Expansions run in ascending or descending powers of three quantities, giving the six Möbius images of x: x, 1/x, 1-x, 1/(1-x), x/(x-1), (x-1)/x. With 4 distinct series each, this gives 24 hypergeometric series (Kummer's 24 solutions organised by Riemann's P-symbol). For any given x at least half of them, i.e. 12, converge.
- In the special cases I, II, III of Art. V (exponent differences admitting extra rational, e.g. quadratic, transformations) these counts are multiplied by 3, 10 and 5 respectively.
- Practical advice: for computation, use the series whose fourth element (the argument) has the smallest modulus.

(4) Integral representations. The integral representation of Art. VII is ∫ s^{..}(1-s)^{..}(1-xs)^{..} ds with endpoints among 0, 1, ∞, 1/x. Applying the transformations of Art. V to it gives representations that are all distinct: 48 in general, and 144, 480, 240 in cases I, II, III. All of them represent the same branch of P, so their ratios are independent of x.
- Within each group of 24, related by an even number of exponent exchanges, the integrals transform into one another by a linear fractional change of the integration variable s. That change sends any three of 0, 1, ∞, 1/x to 0, 1, ∞; there are 4·3·2 = 24 such ordered choices [counting mine].
- The remaining identities, so far as Riemann examined them, need transformations of multiple integrals to verify by integral-calculus methods.
errors: No substantive error. The divergence criterion on |x|=1 is stated loosely. Exactly: F converges absolutely if Re(c-a-b)>0, converges conditionally for x≠1 if -1<Re(c-a-b)≤0, and diverges if Re(c-a-b)≤-1. Riemann's 'order of infinity <1 or >1' matches this, except that conditionally convergent series fail at the single point x=1 itself.
The multipliers 3, 10, 5 for cases I-III depend on the case definitions in Art. V, which are not on this page; they were not re-derived here.

results.what: Convergence of the hypergeometric series on the unit circle governed by Re(γ'-γ) (i.e. c-a-b), with half/all of the 8 expansions converging
results.modern_name: Convergence of 2F1 on |z|=1 (Gauss's criterion / Abel-type boundary behaviour)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1812 (at x=1); boundary behaviour folklore, Riemann 1857

results.what: 24 hypergeometric series representations of a P-function, at least 12 convergent for any x
results.modern_name: Kummer's 24 solutions of the hypergeometric equation

results.what: 48 Euler-type integral representations; 24 of them related by Möbius substitutions of the integration variable fixing three of {0,1,∞,1/x}
results.modern_name: Euler integral representations / Möbius invariance of Pochhammer-type integrals

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed page of Riemann's own published 1857 paper on the hypergeometric function (Art. VIII), with only minor hand annotations. All content is well known and attributed to him.

transcription_corrections: The page is a printed offprint (p. 22 of Abh. Göttingen 7, 1857), not a manuscript. There is a pencilled '11' at top right, a marginal mark (like 'Γr' or 'F') beside lines 4-5, and a '#' in the left margin near the last paragraph.
'niedrigen Ordnung': the print reads 'niedrigen'. A handwritten insertion mark near the final 'n' likely corrects it to 'niedrigern'.
'Integrale betrifft': the 'l' of 'Integrale' is damaged and 'betrifft' is overprinted or bold, with a hand correction mark.
The integration variable 's' at the end of the 'für irgend drei …' line is underlined by hand in red.
